Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence

Financial inclusion in Yemen is not one number.

Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence is a bilingual public evidence resource that helps users understand, compare and verify evidence on financial inclusion in Yemen. It helps decision-making by making clear what the evidence establishes, what it does not, when and to whom it applies, and where it comes from. It does not make decisions for users or simulate policy outcomes. The evidence spans people, firms, providers, payments, money flows, rules and infrastructure, measured at different times and under different definitions. Start with the question you need to answer.

Evidence signals

Three figures, three different things measured

The latest representative population measure is the World Bank’s Global Findex 2021 survey of Yemen (fieldwork November 2022 to January 2023; World Bank data year 2022): 11.9% of adults aged 15 and over in the areas surveyed had an account at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider. Areas holding about 23% of the population were not surveyed. In the same survey, 18.35% of men and 5.44% of women had an account, a gap of 12.91 percentage points. Separately, POS terminals reported by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) rose from 561 in March 2025 to 1,473 in January 2026, within CBY-Aden’s reporting scope. These are different measures: people, a disparity within one survey, and infrastructure. None substitutes for another.

Evidence records behind these figures (4)
  • Latest representative account-ownership measure available
  • A measured gender gap in account ownership
  • POS infrastructure expanded
  • Financial inclusion is a connected system, not a single score
What this does not establish

What should not be inferred?

More infrastructure does not by itself prove that more people are using financial services. A licensed institution is not proof that every listed location is operating. Access does not prove use; use does not prove service quality or impact; and the number of accounts is not the number of people.

Analysis

Different evidence describes different moments.

Population surveys, administrative payment data, provider-status decisions, programme reports and macroeconomic series are updated on different schedules. Each conclusion therefore carries the period it actually covers. “Latest” means latest for that question or measure, not latest for Yemen as a whole.

System context

From rule to result, every link needs evidence.

A reform, new payment rail or programme can matter for inclusion through a chain that runs from a rule or investment to implementation, operation, reachable access, actual use, service quality and protection, and finally outcome. The evidence stops at the furthest stage it actually supports; it does not cross an unmeasured link. Across the wider picture, people and capability, firms and income, providers, payment rails, remittance and capital flows, regulation and consumer protection, and enabling conditions and constraints are related but not interchangeable. Those links show context, dependency or plausible mechanisms where evidence supports them; they are not causal arrows or a composite score.

Another view of the evidence

Financial inclusion is a connected system, not a single score

Text description of this view
  1. Analytical question: How do the parts of Yemen’s financial-inclusion system connect?
  2. What the evidence shows: Financial inclusion in Yemen is described here as connected parts: people and capability, firms and income, providers, payment rails, remittance and capital flows, regulation and protection, and enabling conditions and constraints. The documented relationships describe context, dependency or plausible mechanisms where evidence supports them; no relationship carries an evidence-strength rating, and the parts do not form a composite score or show that one part causes another.
  3. Scope and time: Several periods, varying by domain · people, firms, providers, rails, flows, rules, enabling constraints
  4. What not to conclude: The relationships are not causal claims unless separate evidence supports them; the parts do not form a composite index, and no part is shown to drive another mechanically.

What we still do not know

The gaps the evidence cannot yet close

The evidence available here cannot yet support a reliable national map of operating financial access points, a current population inclusion rate, or a causal explanation for any measured gap. Those are visible knowledge gaps, not values to be filled in.

Verify the evidence

Challenge the answer

Open the evidence record to see the definition, population covered, calculation base, period, geography, method, source, derivation, limitations and what would change it. Where credible figures disagree, compare those fields before comparing the values.

Featured Reading

The system is changing. What has reached people?

Yemen’s rules, institutions and payment infrastructure have moved faster than its representative evidence about people. The gap between the two is not an answer to guess; it is the next thing to measure.

Evidence period: Global Findex fieldwork November 2022 – January 2023 · POS counts March 2025 – January 2026 · institutional records June–August 2026
